blocks.text: The imperfective verb has 3 tenses: the present, the past, and the future. The perfective verb has 2 tenses: the past and the future.

The perfective future consists of one word only and resembles in form the present tense. It is formed from the perfective infinitive: **напишу**, **напишешь** … **напишут**; **сделаю**; **получу**; **выучу**.

In a sentence referring to the future with a subordinate clause introduced by "when" or "as soon as" the verbs of both clauses are in the future: *Я буду читать письма, когда ты будешь учить диалог.* An action of the subordinate clause which is to be completed before the action of the main clause is rendered by the perfective future: *Когда я сделаю уроки, я буду слушать радио. Как только я получу от него письмо, я напишу вам.*
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.
Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: How long will you be staying?
exercises.why: **остаться → останетесь** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: He'll soon catch up with Tom.
exercises.why: **догнать → догонит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: You'll never get anywhere with them.
exercises.why: **сварить → сваришь** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: You just don't get it.
exercises.why: **догонять → догоняешь** — present-type form, 2nd person singular: ending -ешь belongs to the first (е) conjugation.

exercises.prompt: You're going to love this book.
exercises.why: **полюбить → полюбишь** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: What if they kill him?
exercises.why: **убить → убьют** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Put all the rubbish in the barrel.
exercises.why: **положить → Положите** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I will avenge his death.
exercises.why: **отомстить → отомщу** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Беспилотники ___ (пригодиться) для перевозки жизненно важных лекарств.
exercises.prompt: Drones will be useful for transporting life-saving drugs.
exercises.why: **пригодиться → пригодятся** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Никогда не думал, что мы вот так вот ___ (кончить).
exercises.prompt: I never imagined we'd end up like this.
exercises.why: **кончить → кончим** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Изучение клингона сильно ___ (помочь) его карьере бизнесмена.
exercises.prompt: Learning Klingon will be of great use for his career as a businessman.
exercises.why: **помочь → поможет** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: В обозримом будущем мы ___ (смочь) покончить со СПИДом.
exercises.prompt: In the near future, we will be able to put an end to AIDS.
exercises.why: **смочь → сможем** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: We'll do something.
exercises.why: **сделать → сделаем** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Tom is massaging Mary's shoulders.
exercises.why: **массировать → массирует** — present-type form, 3rd person singular: ending -ет belongs to the first (е) conjugation.

exercises.prompt: It'll only make matters worse.
exercises.why: **усугубить → усугубит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I'll drive you somewhere.
exercises.why: **отвезти → отвезу** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Rush hour traffic will start soon.
exercises.why: **начаться → начнётся** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Will Frexit follow Brexit?
exercises.why: **последовать → Последует** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Let's keep an eye on Tom.
exercises.why: **приглядеть → приглядим** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Do you think they'll be offended?
exercises.why: **обидеться → обидятся** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
